statement: You are given a string s made of the characters '(', ')' and '*'.

Each '*' may be read as '(', as ')' or as nothing at all. Return true if some choice for the stars makes s a valid parenthesis string, one in which every '(' is closed by a later ')' and no ')' appears without an earlier unmatched '('. Otherwise return false.

Track the range of possible unmatched '(' counts while scanning: low is the fewest and high is the most. A '(' raises both, a ')' lowers both, and a '*' lowers low and raises high. If high ever drops below 0 the string fails; low never goes below 0. At the end, s is valid exactly when low is 0.

examples.explanation: Reading the star as '(' gives "(())", which is balanced.
Reading the star as nothing leaves "()", which is balanced.
There are three '(' and only one star after them that could close one, so at least two '(' always stay unmatched.
